verses.1: And false teachers also arose among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will introduce deceitful arguments to deceive people. They will refuse to accept anyone who tries to become their leader, thereby causing great harm to themselves.
verses.2: And many will follow in their footsteps, thereby making the path of truth become a road to destruction.
verses.3: And in their excessive and misleading words, they will deceive you. They won’t hesitate to bring about punishment, and their losses won’t be unnoticed either.
verses.4: For indeed, the God of messages did not abandon those who were sinning. Instead, he sent them into judgment, after having scattered them in a state of chaos.
verses.5: And it did not remain in the ancient world; instead, he chose to be a ninth-century prophet of justice. He was chosen to stand against the world’s injustices.
verses.6: And he destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, as an example to those who are cruel and unjust.
verses.7: And Lot, who was wronged by those who were unjust, was driven into exile due to their evil actions.
verses.8: For by sight and by hearing also, the just man lived among them, day after day, and tried to prevent people from doing unjust acts.
verses.9: The Lord knew that the righteous would be tested by trials, but he also knew that those who were unjust would be condemned on the day of judgment.
verses.10: Most of all, those who are driven by lust to engage in such actions, and who disregard authority. They are shameless, arrogant, and not afraid of any consequences.
verses.11: Where messengers who possess great power and strength do not bring upon themselves any unjust judgments.
verses.12: These, being creatures naturally destined to decay and perish, are considered by those who despise them as worthless. In their own decay, they will also perish.
verses.13: They deserve to be punished for their injustice. They claim to enjoy comfort in this world, but they are actually causing harm to others by living in luxury and wastefulness.
verses.14: Having eyes that are capable of seeing the evils that lie within me, and unable to forgive sins; possessing souls that are corrupted by evil thoughts; having hearts filled with greed and selfishness.
verses.15: By following the path of Balam, they were lost. They followed the path that led to Bosor, whom he loved unjustly.
verses.16: He then committed a crime of his own; he hid the falsehoods about the prophet’s words, by distorting them into something that didn’t match their true meaning.
verses.17: These are sources of saltiness, and they are also companions that are being destroyed by the lightning. The darkness of death has been extinguished.
verses.18: For they become increasingly insipid and disgusting as they indulge their desires. This harms those who barely avoid those who are in a state of distraction.
verses.19: They are promised freedom, yet they remain slaves to corruption. For those who resist it, they will be enslaved as well.
verses.20: For if they flee from the troubles of the world under the guidance of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, yet still, when they are caught again, they will be defeated. In that case, their fate will be worse than those who were first caught.
verses.21: For it was difficult for them to understand the path of justice, or to know how to break away from the sacred command that was given to them.
verses.22: It was necessary for them to experience the true taste of suffering. Cylon returned to his own reality, and he became like a worm that was trapped in a trap.
